reference_answer: GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3 was published September 23, 2026. It concerns denial of service through numeric matrix parameters when @angular/router parses attacker-controlled URLs during Node.js/V8 SSR. Angular 22 versions >=22.0.0 and <22.2.0 are affected; 22.2.0 is the first patched 22.x release. Financial HQ UI declares 22.1.7, so its declared package is in the affected range. The pinned source lacks @angular/ssr or @angular/platform-server and no tracked server entry point was found, supporting a client-side assessment, but the snapshot cannot prove deployed topology or reverse-proxy filtering. Verify SSR, URL routing and proxy behavior; if exposed, upgrade the Angular 22 packages together to >=22.2.0 promptly. If confirmed client-only, there is no demonstrated runtime exposure to this advisory, though a normal patch update remains sensible.

sources.title: Angular advisory GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3
sources.snapshot_or_excerpt: Published 2026-09-23, high. @angular/router affected >=22.0.0 <22.2.0; fixed 22.2.0. Preconditions: Node.js/V8 SSR enabled; attacker-controlled request URLs parsed by router during SSR; proxy forwards semicolons and multiple path segments. Numeric matrix parameters amplify V8 heap use and can crash SSR worker. Pure client-side SPAs are unaffected.

facts: The pinned package.json does not declare @angular/ssr or @angular/platform-server.
No tracked server.ts or main.server.ts was found in the pinned tree; the tracked Playwright config starts an Nx client serve target.
The pinned source snapshot does not establish production deployment or proxy filtering.

ambiguities: An affected dependency version does not by itself establish runtime exploitability.
Absence of an SSR dependency or entry point in the pinned tree supports but does not prove a client-only deployment; deployment artifacts and proxy rules may live elsewhere.

must_check: Correct advisory ID, date, package, affected and patched range
DoS mechanism and all material SSR/proxy preconditions
Separation of declared-version finding from confirmed deployment exposure
acceptable_alternatives: Immediate routine update to >=22.2.0 is reasonable even if SSR is unconfirmed, provided urgency is conditional on exposure.
A candidate may recommend a later patched 22.x release instead of exactly 22.2.0 if it states 22.2.0 is the first fix.
do_not_penalize: Saying exploitability cannot be confirmed from source alone
Calling a confirmed client-only deployment unaffected by this advisory

decision_changing_errors: Analyzing a different GHSA in place of GHSA-ff3f-86qr-9cv3.
Calling 22.1.7 fixed or all browser-only Angular apps remotely exploitable.
Presenting SSR deployment or proxy behavior as confirmed without evidence.
